2. Altered the T800 so that it is not bounced around so much by the water
3. Improved the mountain textures on Maupiti
4. Fixed a flickering edge to Maupiti's MFD map image
5. Increased draw distance to 10km

Next week will see the deployment of the main map

notes.title: Map Expansion - Maupiti, French Polynesia
notes.content:
This update adds the French Polynesian island of Maupiti which is situated inside a coral atoll. Access to the island is mainly through a southern passage way between two small sand bank islands although brave captains may be able to find a route through via the northern passage ways as well.

Because of the hidden sand backs and reefs, the MFD map for Maupiti is the 1st map to visually show water depths. Marked depth ranges are <1m, 1m-2m, 2m-3m, 3m-5m, 5m-10m, 10m+

Maupiti is located roughly 6km due East of Ko Lan, I've positioned the initial start position to its main port. The port is tied into the logistics system so missions to and from Maupiti will now be generated.

Next week will see a third island added (almost certainly not a tropical island this time!) as well as the main map (I ran out of time this week!).

I will then make a decision on whether to keep Long Island & Menorca at their current dimensions or resize them down.

Once this is done I think the beta test version can be pushed out into the main branch - finally (unless I decide to add some other stuff first!) :)

Other Updates

1. Corrected the LOD levels for the T800 Oil Tanker which I think was causing dashboard objects to disappear in VR mode.

Happy Boating!

notes.title: Ko Lan Beautification Pass
notes.content:
This is a quick pass to add more detail to the island of Ko Lan. This is also the 1st island to have bushes, ferns and other plants to make up a more forrest/jungle ground cover. I think the effect is quite good.

1. Added palm trees
2. Added jungle ground cover
3. Added sea grass to beach areas
4. Added more detail to underwater terrain to make it less smooth and a little more interesting

The ground cover is currently drawn out to 1km in distance - this may but a lot of strain on VR systems. Please let me know if it has severely impacted your frame rate.

For VR players I will also be re-instating the ability to walk on the terrain so you will be able to explore off the boats again soon...

notes.title: Map Expansion - Ko Lan, Thailand
notes.content:
This update adds a new island, Ko Lan. It's a small island located off the west coast of Thailand, but in the game it is to not too far to the North West of  Menorca. I have set the initial starting point to the new island so you can visit it straight away.

The island has a single pontoon dock serving a small village while the rest of the island is mainly beaches and jungle. The map tile also includes the smaller uninhabited islands of Koh Khrok to the East and Ko Sak to the North. 

The dock itself has a single loading area which is tied into the cargo network so the Quick Job generator will create haulage contracts to and from the new island.

I think this size of island is fairly optimal for the game - it's a good size without it taking too long to travel round it. It is still a work in progress but it is already much closer to what I was aiming for in terms of scenery. I shall continue to add more detail to it over the coming week.

Other updates...

1. Modified the sea renderer slightly so the bottom is a little more visible in shallow water. There should now be a nice smooth transition with bottom visibility starting around the 8m depth point.

2. Added height based fog to the Non-VR camera which should smooth some of the reflection transitions a little. I haven't had time to test it in VR yet hence it is not applied to the VR camera.

3. MFD map for Ko Lan added

4. Map icons/text reduced in size slightly.

Next week will see the addition of another island (possibly another vessel) as well as the global map.

Hopefully I'll then be happy enough to fire this Beta out to the live build!

Happy Boating!

notes.title: Quick Update
notes.content:
I had a bit of spare time today so implemented some changes that I've been meaning to do for a little while...

1. Clamped and re-weighted water drag effects on all boats. This means they shouldn't "bounce" off the water surface if they manage to get significant air time when going over large waves. This also effects the overall motion of the boat when it is being thrown around by waves and also if you manage to flip/crash the boat in the water. The overall motion and effect should look a lot more realistic.

2. Adjusted the ocean reflections, colour and foam distribution so that the ocean is darker with deeper blues. I've upped the resolution of the water reflections and I think it looks a lot more realistic with the water being less blown out with white colouring.

3. Fixed the quit button (again!).

notes.title: New boat and map icons!
notes.content:
This update adds a new boat to the roster - the Flounder! I've also now added place names and icons to the GPS map so you can see where the ports are and any land marks such as light houses etc.

The Flounder isn't quite finished yet, but is driveable in both VR and non-VR modes. The main area that needs work is the wheel house which is a bit ugly at the moment.

The Flounder itself designed to be a starter cargo vessel and is based upon an old fishing vessel that has been converted to carry a wide variety of cargo. It's not fast but it can carry a good amount of cargo in 2 internal and 1 external bays. 

Speaking of cargo and external bays - these are not visually modelled (although weight and centre of gravity calculations are) but they will be soon. This goes for any other vessel that has visible/external cargo bays - soon you'll be able to see the cargo attached to the ship!

OTHER UPDATES

1. Rescaled all cargo sizes to a standard cubic meter (m3) and weights are based on realistic values e.g. 1 m3 of oil is 862kg while 1 m3 of petroleum is 737kg .

2. Ship cargo hold capacities are now calculated in cubic meters and I physically measure hold sizes to make sure they fit inside the 3D model correctly.

3. GPS map now shows ports with names, light houses and other points of interest/landmarks.

4. All textures resized to power of 2 - this not only helps conserve GPU RAM but also graphics drivers don't like them and can cause a GPU crash. You know when this happens as the game will sound like it is still running but the screen will be black or frozen. Let me know if you encounter this happening & if you can remember what you were doing at the time it will help track down any that I've missed!

UPCOMING UPDATES

Next week will be mainly focused on expanding the number of islands to flesh out the cargo network.

Future islands will be around 1/4 - 1/2 the size of the current Menorca island (20km2) - so 5km2 to 10km2. I think this is plenty big enough when some of the vessels only do around 20kts! Islands will still be based on real world terrain - just scaled to fit.

Having smaller islands allows me to not only increase the terrain detail but also the density of objects such as rocks, buildings, trees etc and they also don't take so long to build. I may rescale Menorca and Long Island at some point as well as the actual length of coast line is huge!

I shall also be creating a world map so that you can see the entire area in one go. This will be important when plotting your route between islands as your GPS should NOT be you primary navigation tool especially once GPS/Electrical failures are modelled and the navigation Buoy network is setup! This is fairly true to real life as Captains are taught not to rely on GPS equipment.

Until then - Happy Boating!

notes.title: Quick Job Update
notes.content:
This update adds the Quick Job system to the game.

Quick Jobs can be found in by going Company Info > Job Board > Quick Job

Quick jobs are generated whenever you enter a cargo loading area in a port and will generate random jobs from that loading area to another loading area. Quick jobs are unique as you will be provided with a "hire boat" to complete the job so they are a good way of trying out boats before buying them.

You can cancel a quick job at any time but please be aware that if you save your game while doing a quick job you will lose the "hire boat" when you reload so don't save during a quick job just yet ːsteamfacepalmː

Other things to be aware of - Quick Jobs don't show your destination on the MFD map yet so local knowledge of where the ports are in Menorca is required (you can use a real map if you want).

Sometimes the job generator will create a job between 2 cargo areas in the same port. I will fix this next week but until then it is easy money!

Other Updates...

1. Fixed the floating rocks & lighthouse to the south of Fornells.
2. Tweaked the Mako physics - it still needs some work!

Next week will all be about the boats with at least one new vessel arriving and hopefully some nicer control models for throttle and steering wheel.

I will also be adding in a new map so you can see where the ports are and where your destination port is to aid navigation when doing quick jobs.

I shall also be tweaking the weather system so that extreme weather is less likely and the time between weather changes will be longer and randomised to be a little more unpredicatable.

Once these are in I shall be rolling the current game state out into the main branch. ːsteamhappyː

notes.title: Bug Fixes and Interface Updates
notes.content:
This is a quick update to stomp a few bugs before Friday's main release...

1. Fixed Mouse/Joypad throttle control which would make the engine go full forward when trying to reverse.

2. MFD now shows the map correctly

3. HUD now anchors to the bottom of the screen correctly so it won't appear half way up the screen on resolutions higher than 1080p

4. Hopefully fixed a Unity challenge which would cause the graphics driver to crash when dealing with some textures. This would result in the game hanging visually but you would still be able to hear the boat driving etc. 

5. Added the Quick Job menu which will now display a list of jobs whenever your enter into a docking area. You can't yet select the Quick Job - that's coming on Friday :)

6. Fixed the Quit button so that it actually quits the game now :)

7. Buttons on the boat dash board are now fully clickable in Non-VR mode so, if you wish, you can turn the hud elements off and simply click on the 3D buttons to control everything!

notes.title: Minor Update
notes.content:
This is just a small update to push a few minor but important changes....

1. Changed how the 3rd person camera works. Instead of pivoting up and down near the centre of the boat the camera will now pivot up and down in its local space - it's a bit hard to explain but is a similar system to the one used in "World of Warships" and allows you to look more easily at the horizon and what is around the ship.

2. Altered the physics calculation for rudder force to be correct to real world calculations.

3. Some behind the scenes code for the upcoming cargo missions where you can choose a job and borrow a suitable boat to complete it.

Updates should now return to normal Friday updates. The past 2 weeks I've been busy doing some "real work" on my day job!

Hopefully by the end of next week I will be able to move the BETA to the LIVE branch

notes.title: Bank Account & Renaming Company Update
notes.content:
This update adds the "Bank Account" screen and "Rename Company" screen to the menu system.

The "Rename Company" screen is fairly self-explanatory and allows you to set your shipping company's name.

The "Bank Account" area logs all your transactions so you can see how much you are getting paid for delivering things and what you are spending your money on!

Both of these areas are now stored into the save game system.

Other Updates...

1. Tweaked the "Free Play" start so that all boats are automatically purchased at the start and placed in the "Your Boats" area ready to go.

2. Moved to a proper currency system to store money values. This may cause issues with previous saves.

3. Fixed the clamping of buoyancy which was causing some of the larger boats to sink!

4. Minor button name changes on the Menu System.

This completes the "boring" menu updates for the moment!

Next week I will be working on the "Job Board" area which will generate random missions to carry various cargo using rented boats. This will allow new players to try out various boats and discover new ports while as they get to grips with the game and is a stepping stone before purchasing your own boats (which, at a later date, will require fuel and maintenance to keep running).

Hopefully I will be able to drop in a new boat next week too - probably some kind of smaller starting cargo vessel.

notes.title: Menu System Update
notes.content:
This is a fairly "boring" update as it is focused purely on overhauling the menu system but it also includes a few game updates as well.

1. New menu system with better navigation and buttons!

2. Load and Save system is fully operational! Just 1 save slot at the moment but I will increase that to more in the future.

3. New "Your Boats" area stores all your purchased boats. There are 80 slots and you can own more than one of each boat (important for the future!).

4. There are now 2 different starting states "Normal" and "Free Play"

- Normal mode will give you a Bluefin 24 starting boat and £1,000,000 in the bank to purchase boats you want. The rest you will have to earn from delivering things!

- Free Play gives you the same start but significantly more money. However, you cannot save in this mode. Good for trying out boats before buying them in "Normal" mode.

- I will add extra starting situations as we go forward e.g. "Rags to Riches" for those that want a real challenge etc

5. You can now view your company information screen. Some areas are still under construction, but show what future additions are planned for the game.

6. Physics calculations have had some values clamped to ensure the physics engine doesn't crash when dealing with large numbers. This should also prevent any weird "extreme bouncing" happening if your boat catches too much air.

7. Adjusted the Bluefin's rudder forces and prop steering angle.

Next update will focus on implementing the world map which will show where all the ports are, what cargo they import/export and their various stock levels. 

I'll be looking at adding some smaller cargo vessels to give some progression options to the game as well.

Once this is complete I shall move the beta test into the live version.

After that I shall be revisiting the racing side of things....

Happy Boating!

notes.title: Save Game Update
notes.content:
This update adds a save game system which will save your location, your current boat and also your money so now you can explore the world without having to constantly restart at the same location each time - it does not currently save the industry states so any deliveries you make will be reset each time you start. I will add this information to the save game as soon as I can.

When starting a new game you will be given 2 choices "Normal" or "Free Play". Both are currently very similar with the main difference being a Free Play game cannot be saved.

"Normal" mode will be where the aim of the game is to run your own shipping company and earn money from delivering cargo & passengers and/or discovering hidden treasure.

"Free Play" mode is designed for those who just want to drive the boats around the map without worrying about money.

I should hopefully have the new boat "garage/dock" menu system working which will allow you to buy boats in a "Normal" game. This will replace the current "Swap Boat" area so that it will be possible to buy more than 1 of a certain boat e.g. you can buy multiple Bluefins. This will be useful as some boats will have configuration & upgrade options.

I will also be adding some other Company Management pages to the menu system such as recently completed orders, bank balance etc as well as the ability to name your company and choose a logo...

Other updates...

1. Minor tweaks to the Fury Extreme's physics.
2. Minor tweaks to the Sea Buzzard's physics.

notes.title: Dynamic Clouds and Sea Conditions
notes.content:
Today's update adds dynamic and randomised cloud and sea conditions to the game.

Conditions will currently change every 5 minutes (for testing purposes) and should smoothly interpolate between different states. There is a CPU cost doing this in real-time as the wave spectrum has to be re-calculated for each change but it does run as a second thread so shouldn't impact performance too much.

Sea conditions are based on the "WMO sea state codes" while wind conditions are based on the "Beaufort Scale" and run from Calm all the way up to Phenomenal/Hurricane (14m+ waves!).

You still can't sink a ship but some smaller vessels may get swamped temporarily in big swells. Eventually water egress and bilge pumps will be modelled with the potential for a boat to sink in bad weather :)

Wind conditions are visible in how fast clouds move and roughly determine the state of the sea conditions. However, wind itself is always from the same direction and doesn't effect any of the boats directly just yet - I'll be updating that as soon as I can.

Next week I shall be adding a Weather Forecast screen to the MFD so that you will be able to see both the current and up coming weather and I shall also be adding a fully voiced weather report system that will work through the ships radio along the lines of a BBC Shipping Forecast.

Other Updates...

1. Clouds now cast shadows
2. Clouds now attenuate the Sun, Moon and Stars when they are behind them.
3. Shiny materials should no longer "glow" at night.

notes.title: Hotfix
notes.content: Fixes the 2D control overlay from appearing over the top of the start menu!

notes.title: MFD Map Update
notes.content:
This is just a small update that changes the MFD SatNav Map to a high resolution pre rendered map image.

It's much clearer than the "on the fly" terrain renderer and also much faster for the GPU as it is simply rendering a flat image rather than the actual terrain.

I'll be adding island, Port and other place names to the map together with the cargo accept at each and their various stock levels so you can plan your cargo transportation routes.

I've also fixed a few bugs with the 2D MFD Control Buttons which would highlight incorrectly wwhen you mouse was over an entirely different button!

notes.title: Mouse Control Interface and Minor Changes
notes.content:
This update adds mouse control to the game as well as the ability to tweak the non-VR game hud such as resizing elements or hiding them completely.

Should be fairly familiar to anyone who has played other simulation games...

1. Mouse wheel dollies view in/out (3rd person view only)
2. Hold right mouse button and drag to move the camera view around.
3. To enable mouse driving controls click the "Toggle Mouse Controls" button. This will disable most input from game controllers while mouse controls are active.
4. Use the buttons and sliders to control engine power, steering etc. Bow thrusters only work for ships that have them (currently the Jupiter and T800).
5. MFD can also be controlled via the mouse using the new on screen controls.

Other updates...

1. Bow thrusters now emit a suitable wake/foam when in use.
2. Fixed a lot of errors with engine pivot placements which should mean slightly smoother turning.
3. Adjusted drag effects when hitting the water on most of the boats.
4. Vortex now has an aerodynamic effect when will help keep it pointing in the right direction on large jumps. I've also updated the Vortex's physics so it shouldn't bounce out of the water as much now when impacting waves.

notes.title: New boat and money earning update
notes.content:
Today's update adds another new boat to the game - the Jupiter 130XS which is a 130ft luxury power yacht. It is fully explorable in VR too. Currently it can only be piloted from the fly bridge, but I will be adding internal controls as well.

You can now also earn money from transporting either passengers or cargo around the map. Most ports accept passengers (either standard or VIPs) so they are a good way of making some easy money.

Payment for cargo/passengers is calculated on a base price per unit multiplied by distanced travelled in kilometres. So if you carry 10 VIPs and deliver them 15km away you will be paid £45 x 10 x 15 = £6,750

This calculation will become slightly more complicated as the "prestige" value of the boat used plus your own personal "reputation" value will also be taken into account. This will make doing passenger runs in exotic powerboats boats feasible as their "prestige" value will be a lot higher than other boats offsetting their smaller seating capacities. 

Reputation & Prestige will also come into play once boats can sustain damage/flooding and become sinkable. Losing cargo or passengers will be a bad thing and will reduce your reputation while not maintaining your boat will reduce its prestige value with both values effecting future earnings.

Currently there isn't anything to spend your money on, but the amount is saved so earn your millions now before you have to buy your boats! 

The transportation network will be expanded over the next few weeks.

Other updates...

1. Modifications to all boat physics should make them a little (or a lot!) less stable on the waves.
2. Steering physics have also be tweaked so the forces applied are not instantaneous.
3. Modified the cargo MFD display to show where an item was collected from, how far it has travelled and how much you will make upon transporting it.
4. Moved the Ballast controls to the Boat Settings MFD page.
5. Fixed tree occlusion culling for both standard and VR modes so you should see a bit of a performance increase.
6. Prebaked the ocean masks around Long Island to improve loading speeds.
7. Added a new improved wake system to the Jupiter

Next week will be mostly about populating Long Island, adding extra ports to build up the cargo network and tidying up any left overs such as making light houses work etc.

I'm also hoping that I'll be happy enough with everything to push the BETA into the live build and update the store page to reflect how far this game has come on since it was launched.

notes.title: Long Island Update
notes.content:
This update adds Long Island together with Manhattan Island to the game map.

The island is not fully finished yet, but Manhattan and South Brooklyn Docks are modelled. There are also some other smaller islands including Governor's Island, Roosevelt Island and Mill Rock Park.

I've moved your starting location to the Brooklyn Docks so you have easy access to the new scenery. 

If you want to get back to Menorca you can use the boat reset function which should drop by back at Fornells. However, if you drive directly south from Brooklyn you should hit Menorca within a few minutes (in the Vortex at least!).

Weather conditions are perfect for a quick sprint across the ocean!

Other Updates...

1. Optimised all dock assets.

Next stage will be to get some loading/unloading areas into Brooklyn Docks so that you can at least start to transport people between the two islands.

Transporting people will be slightly different to standard goods as there will be 3 different bonus multipliers in effect...

1. Distance transported - further is always better!
2. Time taken - faster is always better so racing powerboats will do well here even if they can't carry many people.
3. Boat prestige - smarter, more expensive boats will excel here such as the new Luxury Motor Yacht coming soon :)

In addition to this there will be 2 classes of passengers - Standard and V.I.P.s

Not all boats will be able to transport V.I.P.s as it will depend on how fancy they are while others will be able to carry both classes in varying amounts.

Hopefully this should all be implemented in next weeks update...

notes.title: New boat update!
notes.content:
Even though the title of this game is Powerboat VR, there was actually only one real offshore powerboat in the game - the Typhoon.

This update goes a little way to balance this by adding an new Powerboat - the Vortex V390.

It is a V shaped powerboat so provides a totally different experience to the Typhoon.

Other updates...

1. Changed the font on the main menu
2. Split the "Swap Boat" pages into 3 sections to cover Pleasure Boats, Offshore Powerboats & Commercial Boats.
3. Added the Vortex to the boat swap pages
4. Updated the Vortex's "Rooster Tail" generator and the other wake/splash generators to use a different particle system. I think it looks a bit better.

Next update will add a larger boat into the Pleasure Boat category for transporting people around the different islands and hopefully add some new races around Menorca.

Races will initially be more suited to the Offshore Powerboats as they will be longer courses, but I will add some shorter courses for the likes of the Fury Extreme to whip round!

The next phase of development will be to add a new island (probably either Long Island or Manhattan) so that I can setup some longer logistic routes. I've redone the "Road Map" post in the forum so you can see an approximate list of things I will be adding.

Once this is in place I will be pushing the RealWorld Beta "out the door" and into the official build.

notes.title: Non VR Update
notes.content:
This update improves the cameras and views for non-VR users...

1. Added "Toggle Camera Dolly" button (L by default). This allows you to move the camera forward and backwards using the "Player 1 Rotate Cam Y" axis and works in both 1st person and 3rd person views.

2. The 3rd person camera points have been modified so that it is possible to dolly the camera right into the cockpit for a more centred cockpit view, or zoomed right out for a birds eye view.

3. 3rd person view position is maintained when switching between 1st person and 3rd person views.

4. When switching to 3rd person view there will now be a default driver model sitting in the captain's chair - bit better than having a phantom, driverless boat! I will get round to doing some more varied models so you can choose your avatar.

5. When switching to 3rd person view the ocean clipping mask that prevents water from appearing inside the boat will be disabled as it was quite jarring to see a hole in the ocean under the boat from from an outside view.

6. Added keyboard axis camera controls. By default these are mapped to Numpad 2,4,6 & 8. This allows you to swap between camera controls and MFD controls by pressing "Num Lock" (assuming you haven't reassigned anything).

7. Removed some colliders from the ports that were not necessary

notes.title: Industry Background Simulation
notes.content:
This update adds in the background simulation system for island industry.

The simulation runs every "tick" which is currently 30 seconds of real time and processes the production of goods and consumption of materials at each industry site.

This means you can now collect oil from the oil rigs and transport it to the oil refinery at Mahon harbour and it will slowly be converted from oil to fuel.

I've updated the delivery point menu's to show the name of the site and also the stock levels for each item it imports/exports. The levels are indicated by the icon filling up with colour. Items that are empty will appear grey.

There's still no reward for delivering cargo just yet and the storage values will reset each time you start the game, so don't get too invested in hauling cargo just yet :)

Other updates...

1. Upgraded the physics engine for the Fury Extreme. It should feel a bit more lively and shouldn't get bogged down when turning tightly at low speeds. This is a "Jet" boat so there is no rudder - it turns by vectoring the engine thrust so you'll always need to keep power on for it to turn.

2. Adjusted the thottle curve for the Fury Extreme so it should now be easier to drive at lower speeds.

notes.title: Tidy up and bug fix
notes.content:
Quick update to sort out a few challenges I discovered in the current Beta version...

1. Increased LOD level distance to stop buildings etc popping into view at short ranges. Mainly effected VR as the screen ratios are significantly different in that environment.

2. Hopefully fixed the challenge of boat colliders getting in the way of the main menu.

3. Added a dedicated pause button (P or Pause) instead of the game pausing when the main menu was open. This is a work around to fix the main menu sometimes not responding while the game is paused especially if you moved the camera via the seat position adjustment. VR players can pause simply by opening the Steam VR menu.

4. All boat seat positions have been adjusted so that the default position is approximately correct when playing in Non-VR. It should also be close to correct for VR but because you can play standing or sitting it's difficult to make it work for everyone by default.

To combat this, seat position adjustments are now stored on a per boat basis. So you can have a different position for each one. Whenever you swap to a different boat the correct adjustment will be applied straight away so once you've got it all setup you shouldn't need to adjust it again.

This works for both VR and non-VR modes.

5. Non VR interior camera now has motion feedback from the boat. The amount of motion can be set in the seat adjustment menu's lock level. I've set it to a default of 90% which is about right for me. Setting it to 100% will lock you to the boat completely (which is how it was), while 0% will lock the camera to the horizon.

6. Rudder force on the Bluefin has been reduced slighty.

7. Added some mooring buoys to Fornells harbour - (you can't moor to them just yet).

This should leave me clear to work on the logistics side of the game so that I can start hooking up island industries, and also give you rewards for delivering stuff!

The economy will be dynamic so Oil will need to be delivered before Fuel can be refined. Fuel is then needed by the various industries to produce their goods etc. The more in demand an item is the more you'll get for delivering it. Consequently, you won't get the best price if you only deliver one item type continously.

notes.title: Real World Port Update
notes.content:
This is one of the largest updates I've released so far....

1. Resized Menorca down to 1/4 size. Doing a full 1:1 size proved an impossible task - there's just too much coast line. A 1/4 size works rather well and it's now possible to sail around the coast in a sensible time frame.

2. All ports (Mahon, Ciutadella & Fornells) have all been updated to what is, essentially, final production levels. Each port is different and reasonably close to real life layout. The scenery around each port is designed to look pretty rather than being exactly like the real thing.

3. All ports have been optimised as best I can. I think there are probably few LOD levels to sort out to stop things visibly spawning in too much please feedback thoughts in the forum.

4. Fornells now has channel buoys to help show where the deep water is. They currently float but do not have any colliders.

5. Menorca's 3 light houses (Far de Cavalleria, Far de Punta Nati & Far de Favàritx)  are modelled in their correct locations with suitable rocky outcrops etc. They do not yet emit any light at night though.

6. Monte Toro (Menorca's highest point) has been modelled and is visible from Fornells harbour. Should see some lights on it at night too.

7. Changed starting location to Fornells as that's a good place to start exploring from. 

Turn left out of the harbour and you should see one of the light houses (Far de Cavalleria). You can then continue to cruise down the coast to the 2nd light house (Far de Punta Nati) which then leads you round to Ciutadella harbour.

or

Turn right and cruise to the Far de Favàritx lighthouse, continue on to see the oil rigs and then turn right into Mahon harbour.

8. New physics modelling for water impact resistance. There's only two boats that currently make use of this (the Bluefin and the T800) but it now makes the Bluefin an enjoyable ride. You should be able to "feel" the impact into the water which also prevents the boat bouncing out of the water in rougher weather.

9. Fixed the sun so it is now visible!

10. Ocean water wave detail as been increased

11. Ocean water clarity has been reduced just slightly.

12. All harbours have suitable collection/delivery points. These do work but currently you don't get any reward for transporting things - that's my next task!

13. Cave has been removed for the moment due to world rescaling and the fact that it was terribly in-efficient and also broke co-op mode due to lighting issues. It will make a return shortly! :)

14. Minor adjustments to lighting levels and fog levels.

notes.title: Cave Update
notes.content:
This update adds the 1st cave system to the game.

It is located not too far from Mahon harbour. I recommend using the Bluefin to explore it as it is currently the only boat with a light and it gets pretty dark in the caves!

At the moment there is a very noticeable change in the lighting as I have to adjust the ambient lighting to make it dark - I will smooth that out :)

The cave is a reasonable size with multiple routes around it. However, it is fairly sparse as I haven't added any decorations/props.

Other updates....

1. Completely overhauled the rudder system for all boats. Makes a huge difference in low speed manoeuvring and also the boat turns the correct way when going backwards!
2. Tweaked all boat physics so that they handle better on the water. I have also removed all artificial stabilising . This makes it much more interesting and you can dial in the boat's handling by tweaking ballast weight and position.
3. Tweaked ambient lighting.
4. Updated all cargo loading points so they now have the correct import/export items.

notes.title: General Update
notes.content:
This is a bit of a mixed bag of updates!

1. Added passenger collection/drop off points to all the main ports of Menorca

2. Added Oil Drop Off point to Cuitadella Harbour

3. Added Petroleum Drop Off point to Fornells Harbour

4. Added Car/Truck loading point to Cuitadella Harbour (although there are current no ships to use this cargo type....yet!)

5. Readjusted sea renderer so that it is a little less clear and more inline with real ocean water and added Refraction distortion to underwater objects.

6. Fixed some rendering issues with fish so that they are now visible when the camera is under water.

7. Moon is now textured

8. Adjusted day/night lighting to be more realistic. It should now get brighter faster in a morning and fade out quicker at night with more realistic colours.

9. Set up dynamic GPU instancing for terrain trees so that I can turn chunks of them on/off at run time.

10. Readjusted terrain tress to be denser at the coast and none existent further inland where you can't see them. End results is a lot more visible tress with less overhead.

11. Terrain colliders are now disabled when they are not visible.

12. Readjusted cargo loading zones so that they are more transparent and sit lower in the water.

13. Added in extra "non functioning" screens to MFD for RADAR, Treasure Finder, Job Board, Boat Systems and Boat Setup. These screens will get enabled as I build them.

14. All terrain tiles have had their ocean masks pre-rendered so the game now loads much faster. These masks control wave height etc so that shallower water is calmer than deep water.

15. Tweaked the rock colouring to be less dark and closer to "balearic" rock

notes.title: Cargo Pickup/Drop Off Points
notes.content:
Today's update adds a small part of the cargo network to the RealWorld beta branch.

1. Oil can now be collected from the Oil Rigs.
2. Oil can now be delivered to Mahon Harbour.
3. MFD Cargo Management page now has icons to show the current cargo loaded in a specific bay as well as icons showing what cargo each bay can carry.
4. All boats now have a Fuel Tank listed in the Cargo Management page. Fuel usage is not yet implemented but you can load/unload the fuel tank at Mahon Harbour.
5. Ballast tank can be loaded/unloaded anywhere as it is just sea water. However, other cargo types can only be loaded/unloaded at designated places.
6. To load/unload cargo you must get the boat into the defined loading area. It will turn green once you are suitable inside the catchment area.
7. It is possible to overload the ship so be careful :)
8. Loading cargo adjusts the boats centre of gravity so you may need to add ballast to stabilise the boat.
9. The T800 starts with 50% ballast added as it needs this to remain stable. You can pump it out as you load cargo.

Other updates...

1. New music tracks added.
2. T800 physics model adjusted so it doesn't turn as if on rails any more. It will drift slightly as it turns.
3. T800 foam trail increased in length and visible distance
4. Fixed rudder physics which would add speed when turning in reverse.
5. Ocean adjusted so it is not quite so choppy by default. This results in less foam everywhere.
6. Static ships in Mahon harbour now have colliders.

Next week will see the adding of other cargo pickup/drop off points for both the large and smaller vessels and hopefully a new large ferry to pilot. 

I shall also be adding the 1st of many cave systems to explore.

Cave exploring will require the use of the smaller boats and should provide an interesting area to explore with add possibility of finding hidden Pirate treasure amongst other things!

They will also provide tight, technical point to point racing especially as they will be quite dark and will require the use of boat lights to navigate! 

Once the cargo points and cave system are complete I shall be moving the beta test to the live deployment as it will have enough content to satisfy the store page.

Then it will be a case of adding a new island (suggestions welcome) to provide longer distance cargo routes. Speaking of which, I am aware of how slow the larger ships are so I will be implementing a time acceleration system so that longer journeys can be done a little quicker :)

Happy Boating!

notes.title: MFD Update
notes.content:
Today's update adds two new buttons ("+" and "-") to the MFD on all boats.

This extends its capabilities so that various systems (such as loading and unloading cargo or adjusting boat trim) will be controlled via the MFD rather than having to drop out to a menu.

For now though, the "+" and "-" buttons will control the radio volume when you are on the radio page. The selected volume level will be saved when you exit and should automatically be loaded again when you restart the game.

"MFD Plus" and "MFD Minus" can also be defined on the controls section. By default they are mapped to "NUMPAD +" and "NUMPAD -" respectively but you can change that to any key or device button.

This will probably be the last update until next week as I'm away for a few days.

Next week should see the introduction of being able to load oil from the oil rigs and then being able to unload it at one of the harbours on Menorca.

Happy Boating! :D

notes.title: Oil Rigs!
notes.content:
This update adds another part of the cargo delivery network - Oil Rigs. They are currently located just off the coast as you exit Mahon harbour.

These are the starting point of the fuel production chain which will go something like this...

1. [b]Oil Rigs[/b] produce [b]Oil[/b] which needs to be taken to...
2. [b]Oil Refinery[/b] which produces [b]Fuel[/b] which needs to be taken to...
3. Specific island [b]Ports[/b].

The idea is each island requires a certain amount of 3 different items - Fuel, Food and Products. Satisfying all these demands will give a bonus of some sort (not sure what yet!)

Food will be produced by taking a wide variety of items (e.g. fish, meat, vegetables, fruit, grain etc) to a food production hub.

Products are more complicated items that will require a number of items to create (e.g. wood, metal, rubber, electronics etc) but they will also net the most money. For example - to make a car you would need to supply metal, rubber and electronics to a car factory. The factory would then produce cars which can be shipped to other islands/ports for BIG MONEY! 

In addition, the larger the distance from the source to the delivery port the more money you will make per unit giving you an incentive to make the longer trips.

I haven't fully working out all the production chains but I think you can see where I'm going with it :)

Other Updates...
1. Adjusted the T800's engine power so it does a more realistic speed of about 19 knots with slower acceleration.
2. Adjusted the mass and buoyancy properties so it now floats and reacts to waves more realistically
3. Fixed a bug in the rudder calculations that would add a forward force to the object making it accelerate when turning. This effected all boats.

notes.title: Cargo Network Preparations
notes.content:

notes.title: Bow Thruster Update
notes.content:
This is a quick update that adds the bow thrusters to the T800.

They can be triggered via two new buttons to the right of the throttle lever in VR or assigned to button/keys for external controllers such as game pads etc.

The bow thrusters are designed to provide more turning control at low speeds but they can also be used to slowly "crab" the boat into dock by using the thrusters in concert with full rudder lock and main engine power.

I'm not 100% happy with the thruster's VR controls at the moment as keeping your "finger" on the correct button is not easy.

This coming week I shall be working on adding a few more port areas to Menorca so that I can start to work on the transportation routes for ferrying people & cargo around the island.

Once this is setup, I'll start work on a 2nd island to open up longer distance transport routes.

notes.title: Tidy up and bug fixing
notes.content:

1. Adjusted the T800 rudder power so it doesn't turn quite so sharply at low speed.

2. Fixed a collider issue which was preventing you from walking on the main deck of the T800 - you should now be able to access all areas in VR.

notes.title: Rocks and Tree Pass
notes.content:
Today's update...

1. Added fully GPU instanced trees to the terrain. 
2. Added some coast line rock formations around Mahon harbour.
3. Fixed the boat reset position so that you will restart in Mahon harbour correctly and not 50 miles out to sea!

This is a 1st pass at adding some much needed detail to the coast line. Menorca is a volcanic island and has quite a rugged coast line so I am trying to capture that as much as possible.

The rocks are all placed by hand which is quite time consuming, but I think the results look good without causing any major loss of frame rate.

I think it is pretty unrealistic to think I'll be able to cover the entire coast line of an island with these kind of rocks, so each island will have a handful of "Places of Interest" which will be either a port, cove, sea cave, reef or some other kind of area which I shall cover in more detail.

notes.title: Real World Beta Update - Control Rebinding
notes.content:
New update today!

You can now rebind your controls from within the game!

Please note that the control binding menu system only works in Non-VR mode, but once you've configured your controls then they will be used next time you start in VR.

Steering = Left Stick

notes.title: Real World Beta Test
notes.content:
I have now completed the initial terrain generation for the first real world location - the Balearic island of Menorca and you can try it out by opting in to the RealWorld beta

To optin...

1. Right click on "Powerboat VR" in your library and select "Properties"
2. From the new window select "BETAS"
3. Then select "RealWorld - Real World Terrain" from the list.
4. You should then receive a new update for the game.
5. You should choose "Freeplay" from the in game menu as races have currently been disabled and you will start in Mahon harbour.
6. Fish spawning has been increased so you should see more shoals and sharks as you drive around.

The entire island terrain has been imported at a scale of approximately 1:1. So far I have done a 1st pass of the main port of Mahon and a couple of other areas of interest along the inland water way. However, it is possible to circumnavigate the entire island (although there are some odd terrain formations in the sea that I need to fix) and spot the main coves etc but it is quite bland at the moment.

The main focus of future updates will be to populate the main ports of Menorca (Mahon & Ciutadella) and then some of the other main towns and coves. Again, all areas will be approximations of the area using the assets that I currently have so don't expect a true representation with accurate buildings etc - I'm only one person :D

Once these areas have been completed I will be adding a mission board to each port/cove allowing you to pick randomly generated mission using specific boats. Things like...

1. Passenger/Cargo transportation
2. Coast Guard Duties (Boat/Person rescue)
3. Wildlife spotting
4. Treasure hunt
5. Finding places of interest

I will also be adding some different boats into the game such as larger powerboats, super yachts, ferries & cargo ships to add a lot of variety. Other water craft such as hovercraft, sail boats, canoe's and jetskis are all possible but the change in physics mean they will be coming later in development and I can't rule out that they will need to be paid DLC - it really depends on how well the game sells...

Other islands will be added to give an "Ultimate Hits" of boat driving areas with enough space for the BIG boats! So, no matter what boat your driving - from a tiny Canoe all the way up to a Super Container Ship - you should be able to find the perfect place :)

Other things I want to add...

1. Buoy navigation
2. RADAR
3. Weather systems
4. Tidal/Water flow
5. AI boats
6. Boat damage

This should show the direction this game will be going i.e. a more encompassing, realistic, simulation rather than just a racing game. 

Racing will still feature but, at least for the moment, it will take a lesser priority.

As always, please join in on the forums as your ideas and suggestions really are driving this game!

notes.title: Race Option Update 1
notes.content:
This is a straight to live update. Please ensure that you opt-out of any Betas.

This update if focused on configuring races and so allows you to select your sea conditions, time of day and AI level when starting a Quick Race.

[u][b]SEA CONDITIONS[/b][/u]
Sea conditions are broken down in to approximate Beaufort levels from Calm all the way up to Hurricane. Rougher sea conditions will make racing a lot more challenging. Sea conditions will remain after the race has finished so, for the moment, you can use it to set sea conditions for free play by starting a race and then quitting. I will add sea conditions to the main menu shortly.

[u][b]TIME OF DAY[/b][/u]
Time of day is pretty self explanatory and allows you to race at any time of day. Night racing can be tricky as the checkpoints are not easily visible. I will be updating the checkpoints with lights and an indicator to make visual "Mk1 Eye Ball" navigation easier rather than having to rely on the Sat Nav.

[u][b]AI LEVEL[/b][/u]
AI level can also be adjusted from 50% to 150%. This value currently only effects the power the AI's boat produces. So at 150% they will produce 50% more power than your boat and at 50% they will have half your engine power. 

However, their top speed will still be limited to the same level as it does not effect prop/engine RPM values they will just accelerate quicker and hold speed in tight corners better. I would recommend incrementing the value slowly by +-5% depending on whether you want more or less of a challenge. High values may cause the AI's boats to behave unexpectedly.

notes.title: Mega Physics Update
notes.content:
Ahoy there, Skippers!

I am very pleased to announce that the new physics engine is now live. I can thoroughly recommend checking out the boats and having a go at the races. Definitely try out the "Typhoon" racing catamaran if nothing else!

The new physics make the boats much more lively and will take some skill to control correctly - case in point would be the Typhoon which can get a little out of shape even in a straight line.

Here's a quick break down of the boats and how they handle...

1. Buzzard - A fairly heavy day cruiser/powerboat. It handles well in all conditions and is perfect for new boaters.
2. Mako - Newly uprated engine makes this R.I.B. a beast to handle well. Not really suited for rough weather as there's a real risk of flipping it over!
3. Bluefin - Excellent handling and as happy skimming along the top of the water as it is flying through the air.
4. Fury - quick and light and can be a handful in rough conditions as it will likely "chine walk" if pushed too hard.
5. Typhoon - all out, bonkers quick, racing catamaran/tunnel hull. Will hit 115kts+ in flat water and has a tendency to powerslide in turns which can be bad news if you catch a wave at the wrong time.

Feedback on the boat handling is, as always, very welcome.

notes.title: Mega City Update!
notes.content:
Ahoy There, Skippers!

This update introduces the "Mega Cities" that I've been working on. No longer will a city be made up of just 10 buildings! Now they stretch along the coastline much like real cities do with smaller buildings on the outskirts and towering skyscrapers towards the middle and is much closer to what I had in mind for the game.

They are still procedurally generated so you may well see things like trees stuck inside buildings etc but I'll get round to fixing those at a later date. For now it provides a fantastic background for boating!

You'll also notice that even though the cities are now huge performance isn't reduced by much and in some areas it will be better. The game now tends to run at a higher frame timing - but it is more constant. 

The starting location is actually one of the highest density areas of the map as 4 terrain/city tiles are in view at once so it's a good bench marking site.

There are still optimisations to be done and almost certainly I will need to split the cities into detail levels to reduce overall density to help out lower spec'd machines.

Please ensure you are "opted in" to the BETA branch to get this update.

notes.title: 900km2 of Tropical Islands to Explore - BETA TEST
notes.content:
Ahoy There, Skipper!

I am very pleased to announce that the new 900km2 (30km x 30km) island map is now ready for you to test.

I have launched it as an opt-in beta test so for those who don't know how to opt-in to these things please follow the instructions below...

1. Go to your Steam library and find Powerboat VR
2. Right Click on it and go to properties
3. A window will pop up, click "BETAS"
4. From the drop down you will be able to select "betatest - Map Beta Test"
5. Close the window and Steam should schedule an update for Powerboat VR which should be 2.2Gb in size.
6. Once it has downloaded you can run the game and enjoy the new map.
7. If you want to revert back to the old version just repeat these instructions but select "None" from the BETA drop down.

BAD POINTS (Hence the beta release)
Loading time is quite slow - it can take a while before everything loads ok so please be patient. I've already fixed this but haven't had time to rebuild everything for release. Expect an update tomorrow.

First of all there is definitely a performance hit on the new map - not huge but it may be enough to cause reprojection on some machines. As a guide my test system (i9-9900k / RTX2080ti) I get around 7.5ms - 8ms when driving around the map. in a race this increases to around 11ms - 12ms, enough to cause some reprojection. However, there is plenty of optimisation to be done on the new map so I am quite sure this will come down in future updates.

The new map contains the same number of races and delivery points but they are now spread out a bit more because of the map size change. This makes the MFD map somewhat difficult to use as the icons and names get too small to read and the map doesn't zoom out far enough to see much more than the 1st island. I will try to fix this tomorrow.

GOOD POINTS
It's a new map - and it's huge. You start off in the roughly in the middle of the map so you have 15km in any direction to explore. I'd estimate that even using the Typhoon and hitting its maximum speed of 100kts it will still take about an hour to circumnavigate the edge of the map let alone visit the interior islands!

The whole area has been covered with new high resolution textures both on land and beneath the sea. While the terrain itself has been modelled more realistically with lovely smooth beaches sloping gently into the sea. The fish also react to the new terrain better as the depth is more constant so they know where to swim. They can still clip through the ocean floor though (another thing to fix!).

The race tracks length have been increased so they are more suitable for powerboating. The races now last longer and, trust me, you'll need the extra length if you are going to beat the new race AI which has had a bit of an upgrade. They're still a bit dumb in situational awareness (I'll be fixing that shortly) so they do tend to collide but they now haul ass and are just as fast as you. Please remember that the AI uses an identical copy of the boat you are in, physics and all, so if they beat you it's not because they cheated! ;o)

I have modified the ocean waves so they are slightly smoother and they also flow a bit slower mimicking the swell of an ocean a bit better. This also gives you a little more time to react to large waves and have at least an attempt at steering round them which will be important shortly because...

The new engine/boat management system will hopefully be coming next week. This update will mean the end of just holding the throttle open and hoping for the best. You'll need to manage your engines by reducing revs when props come out of the water as well as choosing the gentlest racing line where possible to reduce damage to the boat and yourself! Expect things like water ingress, mechanical failures, electrical failures and also a simulation of the physical punishment you are experiencing. These will all be togglable with varying levels so you'll be able to configure the game to your preferences.

notes.title: Control Update
notes.content:
Ahoy There, Skippers!

As part of the control system update I have added a hybrid VR control setup to the game. This system allows you to control the boat using your VR controllers rather than having to actually grab the controls.

I actually prefer driving the boats like this.

In each boat there is a new GREEN button which toggles the "Remote Control" system on and off. With it switched on you can apply throttle with the trigger and steer with the thumbstick/touch pad. You can still grab the controls if you want allowing e.g. if you want to steer using the virtual controls but like the throttle on the trigger then you can do this. 

Please note that there is currently no reverse on the triggers and that when the "Remote Control" system is on the virtual VR controls will re-centre after being released rather than stay where they are with the system off.

In the next day or so I should complete the rest of the control update which will allow you to configure pretty much any physical control system to control the boat e.g. Wheel, pedals, joypad etc.

notes.title: Cargo Mission Update
notes.content:
Ahoy There, Skipper!

The new update today includes a total overhaul of the cargo delivery system.

Instead of a random system, each cargo collection point will have a selection of different "Missions" for you to complete. These missions are curated so that everyone gets the same cargo, same weather and the same boat to complete it and they each have a little back story and may even involve you getting off your boat!

At the end of the mission you will be awarded a score & rank based upon the cargo you delivered and how fast you did it.

These scores are saved locally but will be uploaded to a Steam Leaderboard in the future.

Boat physics have also been tweaked and a new volumetric fog system has been added while the ocean wave system's detail has been improved and now uses the Beaufort Scale to match waves to weather conditions.

As always, you are invited to the Powerboat VR Steam forums to give feedback and post ideas and, with this new update, ideas for missions would be most welcome!

Happy Boating!

notes.title: Physics & Content Update
notes.content:
New updated released today that includes updated physics modelling and a new powerboat.

Additional Content
1. Fury Extreme powerboat - a small jet boat that is both light and fast. It is unlocked at 2,000xp although for early access it is available from the starting beach.

Physics Update
1. Updated the physics modelling to include a much better planing system. 
2. General buoyancy of each boat has been updated so they don't sink as easily when loaded with cargo.
3. Buoyancy and planing forces have been modified to prevent excessive bouncing/pop off the waves. Mainly effects the larger boats which would get airborne a little too easily.

Fixes
1. Fixed an issue where you wouldn't be able to switch to a new boat via the tablet's rewards screen.
2. Fixed the finger point gesture zone on the Bluefin so that it won't activate when grabbing the steering wheel.

This update now finalises the overall physics system which means I can move on creating new content!

The primary focus of the next few updates will be reworking the cargo delivery system so that it works around pre-set "missions". These will take the form of point-2-point rally races against the clock. Each mission will be require you to delivery cargo, amongst other things, in a set boat with specific time of day/weather conditions. Scores will then be shared on a world wide leader board.
